passage:
Family counsellor's note, third session: Chandrika and her son Sachin (16).
Today they drafted an agreement together, and both signed it. Terms: Sachin shares any evening plan by 4 pm the same day, with who and where. He replies to one check-in message if he's out after eight. Chandrika agrees to give a real answer, not an automatic no, and to say yes when the plan is honest and safe. Review date: 30 September, here. Sachin asked, "What if you still say no to everything?" Chandrika said, "Then you can bring that up at the review." He looked surprised, then nodded. Mood noticeably lighter than last session; they left joking about who would forget first.

qa.q: By what time must Sachin share an evening plan?
qa.a: He shares any evening plan by 4 pm the same day.

qa.q: Why did Sachin look surprised when his mother answered?
qa.a: He had expected his worry to be brushed aside, so he was surprised she agreed he could raise it at the review.

qa.q: Why is a review date useful in this agreement?
qa.a: It makes trust-building visible and checkable, and gives both a fair time to adjust the rules instead of arguing.

qa.q: What does Chandrika commit to, and how might that feel for Sachin?
qa.a: She commits to real answers and to saying yes to honest, safe plans, which may make Sachin feel that honesty will actually pay off.

grounding: Shows a parent and teen agreeing small, specific rules with a review date, with the parent committing to say yes more when the teen is honest.

passage:
Tuesday
So Abbu and I made a deal tonight. It's written on the back of an old calendar page and stuck on the fridge (Ammi's idea). Rules: I tell them plans a day ahead. I send a photo when I reach. If I'm going to be late, I call, not text. In return, Abbu said he'd say yes more when I'm upfront, and actually mean it. We look at it again on the 15th. First test: Naveen's cricket match on Saturday. I asked yesterday, not on Saturday morning like I usually would. Abbu said yes!! Just like that. Then he patted my head like I was his little boy again. Weird feeling. I think I've been lying so long I forgot asking could work.
— Farhan

qa.q: When will they look at the deal again?
qa.a: They look at it again on the 15th.

qa.q: What does Farhan realise at the end of the entry?
qa.a: He feels surprised and a bit strange, realising he had been lying so long that he forgot asking could actually work.

qa.q: What made the first test go well?
qa.a: Farhan asked a day ahead as agreed, and Abbu kept his side by saying yes to an honest plan.

qa.q: How might Abbu feel when Farhan asks about the match a day early?
qa.a: Abbu likely feels reassured and trusted, which makes it easier for him to say yes and mean it. 🙂

grounding: Shows a teen and his father agreeing clear rules with a review date, and the father saying yes to an honest request as promised.

On the verandah of their house near the tea gardens, Naveen and his mother Sudha sat with a notebook between them.
"Write it down," Sudha said. "So we both remember."
Naveen wrote: "One. Tell Amma where I'm going and with whom, before leaving. Two. Be home before the temple bell at seven. Three. If late, call from Raju's shop phone."
Sudha added: "Four. Amma will say yes more often, if Naveen asks honestly."
Naveen looked up. "You'll really say yes?"
"If you tell me the truth, yes, more often. We'll look at this notebook again after Pongal."
Naveen underlined rule four twice.

qa.q: When will Naveen and Sudha look at the notebook again?
qa.a: After Pongal.

qa.q: What was Naveen feeling when he asked "You'll really say yes?"
qa.a: He was hopeful but doubtful, not quite believing that honesty would lead to more yeses.

qa.q: What makes this agreement a clear path back to trust?
qa.a: The rules are small and specific, with a review date, and Sudha commits to saying yes more often when Naveen is honest.

qa.q: What might Sudha be experiencing as Naveen underlines rule four?
qa.a: She probably feels touched and hopeful, seeing how much that promise means to her son.

grounding: A teen and his mother write small, specific rules with a review date, and she commits to saying yes more when he is honest.

passage:
In the kitchen of their flat in Buenos Aires, Camila and her mum stuck a sheet of paper on the fridge.
"Plans shared by Thursday for the weekend. Home by ten, or text by nine thirty. Location on when out late."
Underneath, her mum had added in her own handwriting: "If Camila asks honestly, Mum will try to say yes more often."
"And we look at this again at the end of the month," her mum said.
Camila read it twice. "So if I ask to sleep over at Mei's on Saturday?"
"Did you tell me by Thursday?"
"It's Wednesday."
Her mum smiled. "Then yes."

qa.q: What day did Camila ask about sleeping over at Mei's?
qa.a: On Wednesday.

qa.q: What was Camila feeling when she read the sheet twice?
qa.a: She seemed hopeful and a little unsure, testing whether the new rules would really lead to yes.

qa.q: Why does this approach help rebuild trust?
qa.a: The rules are small, specific and visible on the fridge, with a review date, and the mum commits to saying yes more when Camila is honest.

qa.q: What might Camila's mum be experiencing when she smiles and says yes?
qa.a: She probably feels pleased and relieved that Camila followed the new rule, and glad to keep her side of the deal.

grounding: A teen and her mum agree specific rules with a review date, and the parent commits to saying yes more often when the teen is honest.

The counsellor's office at Naveen's school had a round table instead of a desk, which Yogesh noticed as he sat down next to his son.

"So," said Mrs Dias, "last week we talked about why the lie happened. Today, let's make it concrete."

They wrote it together on one sheet. Naveen shares weekend plans by Thursday night, including who and where. He texts when he arrives and when he leaves. Yogesh, in turn, would say yes to at least one outing a week if the plan was clear, and give reasons if he said no.

"Review date?" Mrs Dias asked.

"End of the month," said Naveen.

Yogesh hesitated, then signed his part first. "I'll hold up my end," he said. Naveen looked at his father's signature for a long moment, then signed his own.

qa.q: By when must Naveen share weekend plans?
qa.a: Naveen shares weekend plans by Thursday night.

qa.q: What might Naveen have felt when his father signed first?
qa.a: Naveen probably felt surprised and a little hopeful, seeing his father commit to his part of the deal.

qa.q: Why does this written plan help rebuild trust?
qa.a: It sets small, specific rules with a review date and asks the father to say yes more often, so trust can grow in visible steps on both sides.

qa.q: How might Yogesh feel after signing?
qa.a: Yogesh may feel uneasy about letting go, but also hopeful and committed to showing that honesty will be rewarded.

grounding: In a school counsellor's office, a parent and teen agree specific rules with a review date, and the parent commits to saying yes more often.
